channel.title: The Colorado Sun - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Colorado Sun (coloradosun.com)

item.title: Mikaela Shiffrin arrives at her fourth Olympics hardly burdened by the ghosts of Beijing
item.description: Shiffrin left China without a medal, crashing out in three races and failing to reach the podium in three othersv

item.title: After saying goodbye in 2025, Denver’s largest music festival is back on in a new neighborhood
item.description: The Underground Music Festival, which spent the past two decades bouncing around South Broadway, will reappear this summer in RiNo

item.title: 134 more people laid off from federal renewal energy lab in Golden
item.description: National Laboratory of the Rockies, formerly NREL, keeps shrinking under Trump administration changes

item.title: Laura Clellan, tapped as interim Colorado Parks and Wildlife boss, named sole finalist for the permanent job
item.description: Clellan, a retired Army commander, brings decades of leadership in fraught circumstances that allies say will help steady the state agency

item.title: How one man learned his mother was found among 189 decaying bodies at a Colorado funeral home
item.description: Hundreds of families learned from officials that the ashes they ceremonially spread or kept close weren’t actually their loved ones’ remains. The bodies of their mothers, fathers, grandparents, children and babies had moldered in a room-temperature building in Colorado.

item.title: The Colorado Symphony just had its Super Bowl in NYC. But is $70,000 a year enough to keep musicians on the field?
item.description: Symphony CEO Daniel Wachter says he’s sweetening the pot for orchestra musicians with collective bargaining agreements

item.title: Colorado farmers would need “prescription” to use common pesticide if legislature passes environmental bill
item.description: Growers worry the bill, backed by the governor, will add bureaucracy and cut yields and profits. Advocacy groups say neonicotinoids are being used as an insurance policy.

item.title: National Democrats see a path to winning Colorado Springs’ congressional seat for first time ever
item.description: The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee announced that the 5th Congressional District is now on its list of “districts in play.” The designation may eventually come with money.

item.title: A top Democrat in the Colorado Senate is resigning to take nonprofit job, citing legislative pay
item.description: Senate President Pro Tempore Dafna Michaelson Jenet of Commerce City, who spent nearly a decade at the Capitol fighting for sexual assault survivors and to improve mental health care, said serving in the legislature has become a financial hardship for her family

item.title: Why your Colorado property tax bill still increased this year
item.description: The state had granted temporary tax discounts in recent years, but they are expiring. At the same time, tax rates paid to schools are also effectively increasing.
